bull_thesis: The catalyst resolves favourably if two things happen together: the magnet build-out lands on schedule and the rare-earth scarcity premium comes back. Both are live. MP Materials is the only fully integrated rare-earth producer in the United States, and in July 2025 the Department of Defense (now the Department of War) made it a national champion by contract: a $400 million preferred investment convertible at $30.03 a share, a ten-year warrant at the same strike taking the government to roughly 15% of the company, a $150 million loan for heavy rare-earth separation, a $1.0 billion construction facility arranged by JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs, a ten-year guaranteed floor price of $110 per kilogram on neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr, the key magnet input) that began in October 2025, and a commitment to buy 100% of the magnets from the new plant for ten years with a minimum $140 million a year of operating cash profit. Apple added a $500 million recycled-magnet agreement, with shipments starting in 2027, and General Motors is an offtake partner. Execution has been genuinely good: first magnets rolled at the Independence plant in Fort Worth in December 2025, first-quarter 2026 NdPr output was a record 917 metric tons (up 63% year over year) on sales of 1,006 tons (up 117%), revenue rose 49% to $90.6 million, and the 200-ton dysprosium and terbium circuit at Mountain Pass is on track to commission in mid-2026, which would make MP one of only two sources of separated heavy rare earths outside China. interrogator_dossier:
# MP Materials (MP) - Event-Driven Forensic Dossier

Reviewed 3 August 2026. Special-situation lens: the thesis is the spread between today's
price and an event-resolved value, not business quality. The questions that matter are
whether the catalyst is real, dated and binding; how credible the sponsor is on hitting
it; and what actually backstops the price if the event does not arrive.

All prices and figures below were verified against live sources on 3 August 2026 and are
dated in-line. Where the board's stored dossier disagreed with the tape, the tape wins.

---

## 0. What changed since the board file was written

The stored board entry carried a live price of $45.24, a target of $82 and a floor of $35.
Two of those three no longer hold up.

| Field | Board file | Verified 3 Aug 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live price | $45.24 | **$41.37** (close, Friday 31 July 2026; traded $40.72-$43.40 on 2 Aug) | live quote |
| Street target | $82.00 | $80.70 consensus / $81 median, range $69-$100, but being cut (JPMorgan to $60 from $75 on 29 July 2026) | consensus feed |
| Downside floor | $35.00 | Not supported by assets. Book value is $11.07 a share; net cash is about $3.88 a share | balance sheet |

The stock is now 59% below its 52-week high of $100.25 and only 9% above its 52-week low
of $37.81. The 50-day average is $54.64 and the 200-day is $59.21, so the shares are
trading roughly a quarter below their own medium-term trend. This is a name in an active
de-rating, not a name at rest.

---

## 1. Is the catalyst real, dated, and binding?

The board labels the driver "supply timing" and marks it undated. That label is correct,
and the reason matters.

**The binding, contractual events already fired.** In July 2025 the Department of Defense
(now the Department of War) signed a partnership that gave MP Materials a $400 million
preferred-equity investment convertible at $30.03 a share, a ten-year warrant at the same
$30.03 strike taking the government to roughly 15% of the company, a $150 million loan for
heavy rare-earth separation, and a $1.0 billion construction facility arranged by JPMorgan
and Goldman Sachs. Apple added a $500 million recycled-magnet agreement in the same month.
Every one of those is signed, closed and in the price. There is nothing left to announce.

**What remains is a construction schedule, and it lands in 2028.** The 10X magnet campus in
Northlake, Texas broke ground during the first quarter of 2026; it is budgeted above
$1.25 billion, will run about 7,000 metric tons of magnets a year, and produces its first
commercial product in 2028. Together with the 3,000-ton Independence plant in Fort Worth,
that gets the country to roughly 10,000 tons a year of magnet capacity, but not before
2028-2029. Apple deliveries begin in 2027. A multi-year construction ramp is not a dated,
binding event; it is a story with a schedule that can slip.

**The one genuinely hard date inside the window cuts both ways.** China suspended its
October 2025 rare-earth export-control package for one year, and that suspension expires on
**10 November 2026**. Three outcomes are on the table: extension, selective reinstatement,
or full reimposition. Reimposition would be strongly favourable for MP Materials, because
the entire western scarcity premium rebuilds. Extension, which is the market's working
assumption after the Beijing summit thaw, is the bear case, and it is the outcome that
already knocked the shares down more than 10% in a single session on 18 May 2026 when a
bilateral deal looked close. A dated coin-flip whose bad side is live is not the asymmetric
catalyst this funnel is built to buy.

**The nearest date of any kind is second-quarter results on 6 August 2026**, confirmed by
the company on 16 July 2026, after the close, with the call at 5:00 p.m. Eastern. That is a
data point on the ramp, not a thesis-resolving event.

One live negative also belongs here: on 22 June 2026 China's Ministry of Commerce added MP
Materials to its own export-control list, banning shipment of Chinese dual-use goods to the
company. The shares fell 13.4% over the month. Management's position is that its Chinese
dependencies were already largely eliminated, so the direct commercial damage is limited,
but it removes any residual optionality on Chinese equipment or feedstock.

**Verdict on the catalyst: real, but soft and long-dated.** The value-realising milestone is
in 2028. The only firm date inside twelve months is a third-party geopolitical binary whose
consensus outcome is the unfavourable one.

---

## 2. Sponsor and management credibility

**Operationally, credibility is high.** First-quarter 2026 production of neodymium-
praseodymium (NdPr, the key magnet input) was a record 917 metric tons, up 63% year over
year, on sales of 1,006 tons, up 117%. Total rare-earth oxide production reached 12,983
tons. Magnet manufacturing began at Independence in December 2025 and the Magnetics segment
already turned $21.1 million of revenue into $9.6 million of segment-level operating cash
profit in its first full quarter. Heavy rare-earth separation at Mountain Pass, a 200-ton-a-
year dysprosium and terbium circuit fed by stockpiled concentrate, is on track to commission
mid-2026. This is a management team that has hit its physical milestones.

**On the ownership side, credibility is weaker, and this is the single sharpest forensic
flag in the file.** The chairman and chief executive, James Litinsky, has been a persistent
and heavy seller through the de-rating. His revocable trust sold roughly 400,900 shares for
about $26.2 million between 27 and 29 May 2026, a further 185,167 shares for about
$12.8 million on 3 June 2026, and filed additional intent-to-sell notices covering 150,000,
200,000 and 250,000 shares across April and May. Reported insider selling exceeded
$43 million in a single quarter and has continued since. Selling into a 59% drawdown, by the
person with the best view of the construction schedule, is not what a manager does when he
believes a near-term milestone will re-rate his stock. It is entirely consistent with the
read that the payoff is in 2028 and the interim is going to be uncomfortable.

---

## 3. The verified downside floor

This is where the board's file is most wrong, and it is the reason the setup fails.

**There is no asset floor near $35.** Verified balance-sheet facts: cash and short-term
investments of $1.74 billion at the end of the first quarter of 2026, total debt of about
$1.05 billion, enterprise value of $6.67 billion, and book value of $11.07 a share on
178.0 million shares. Net cash is therefore about $690 million, or $3.88 a share. A $35
floor is roughly 3.2 times book value and nine times net cash. Nothing on the balance sheet
holds the price there.

**There is, however, a real floor on the cash flow, and it is contractual.** The Price
Protection Agreement with the Department of War guarantees $110 per kilogram of NdPr for ten
years, commencing October 2025, paid quarterly as the shortfall between $110 and the
benchmark volume-weighted average price, on every kilogram produced, including material
consumed internally in magnet manufacturing and material merely stockpiled. It contributed
$42.3 million of income in the first quarter of 2026 alone. On a roughly 4,000-ton annual
NdPr run-rate that mechanism underwrites something on the order of $440 million of annual
gross NdPr value regardless of what China does to the spot price. Separately, the government
guarantees a minimum of $140 million a year of operating cash profit at the 10X facility for
ten years once it runs, and commits to buy 100% of its output.

So the correct statement is: the Department of War has floored the **cash flow**, not the
**share price**. That is genuinely valuable and it is why this will not go to zero. It is
not the same thing as a deal-break price or a cash-per-share backstop, and it does not
prevent a multiple de-rating from taking the equity to $30 or below.

**A defensible floor is about $29, not $35.** Three anchors converge there: the government's
own $30.03 conversion and warrant strike, which is the price at which the largest shareholder
bought; roughly 2.5 to 2.8 times book value, which is where a contracted-cash-flow miner with
a stalled growth story would find support; and a capitalisation of the price-protected
materials business alone at about $180 million of operating cash profit on a mid-single-digit
to nine-times multiple. The stock has already printed $37.81 in the last year. Assuming the
line holds at $35 requires believing the drawdown stops eight per cent below where it just
stopped.

---

## 4. The undisclosed catch in the contract structure

The Department of War did not simply de-risk the downside. It bought a large share of the
upside, and this is not visible in the headline terms most write-ups quote.

- On NdPr, when the market price exceeds the $110 floor, **the government receives 30% of
  the surplus.** At today's roughly $133 per kilogram alloy benchmark, MP Materials keeps
  $110 plus 70 cents on each surplus dollar, not the full spot price.
- On the 10X magnet facility, the arrangement is cost-plus with a guaranteed $140 million
  minimum. Commercial sales profits above the first $30 million over that baseline are
  **split fifty-fifty** with the government.

The practical consequence: 10X is structurally closer to a regulated utility than to a
merchant magnet business, and Mountain Pass keeps only 70% of any scarcity spike. Any model
that capitalises unshared merchant magnet margins on 7,000 tons of 10X capacity is
overstating what accrues to common shareholders. This is the specific mechanism by which a
street target near $80 is too high, and it is verifiable in the deal documentation rather
than a matter of opinion.

---

## 5. The financial reality underneath the story

The narrative is national-security scarcity. The numbers are those of a pre-revenue
industrial build-out.

| Measure | Trailing twelve months, verified 3 Aug 2026 |
|---|---|
| Revenue | $347.6 million |
| Operating cash profit (EBITDA) | **negative $132.0 million** |
| Net income | negative $71.2 million |
| Operating cash flow | **negative $94.5 million** |
| Enterprise value to sales | 19.2 times |
| Price to book | 3.74 times |

The first quarter of 2026 was reported as a $36.6 million operating cash profit, but
$42.3 million of that was the government price-protection payment. Strip the subsidy and the
underlying business ran slightly below breakeven at the operating-cash-profit line while
spending heavily on 10X. That is not a criticism of the strategy; it is the honest starting
point for anyone paying 19 times sales.

---

## 6. Red flags and green flags

**Concerning**
- The chairman and chief executive sold roughly $58 million of stock between April and June
  2026, into a collapsing share price.
- The claimed $35 floor is unsupported by assets: book value is $11.07 and net cash is $3.88
  a share.
- Trailing operating cash profit is negative $132 million and operating cash flow is negative
  $94.5 million while capital spending on 10X runs above $1.25 billion.
- The government takes 30% of NdPr upside above the floor and half the 10X commercial profit
  above a threshold, capping the bull case in a way most models miss.
- Nineteen times sales for a business whose principal plant does not produce until 2028.
- Added to China's export-control list on 22 June 2026.

**Encouraging**
- The only fully integrated rare-earth producer in the United States, with the government as
  its largest shareholder and a ten-year contracted price floor. That combination is not
  replicable by a competitor.
- Every physical milestone has been hit: first magnets in December 2025, record NdPr output
  in the first quarter of 2026, heavy rare-earth separation commissioning on schedule for
  mid-2026.
- The commodity is working. NdPr reached a 2026 high near $133 per kilogram on 1 July 2026,
  more than double the roughly $53 level at which the year began, after a V-shaped recovery
  from a June trough near $90. The equity is at a 52-week low while its main product is at a
  yearly high, which is a genuine dislocation and the strongest single argument for the name.
- Short interest is roughly 16% of shares outstanding, about 28.9 million shares. Any
  favourable surprise has fuel behind it.
- No secular force threatens the terminal value. Defence reshoring and electrification are
  tailwinds, and the price-protection agreement blunts Chinese price warfare specifically.

---

## 7. What the market is arguing about

The bull says: the commodity has doubled this year, the plants are funded and on schedule,
the government owns 15% at $30.03, short interest is 16%, and the shares are 59% off the
high. That is a real argument and it deserves respect.

The bear says: the equity is not cheap on anything you can measure today, the payoff year is
2028, the government has pre-sold a third of the upside, the chief executive is selling, and
the only hard date before then is a Chinese policy decision on 10 November 2026 whose
consensus outcome is the unfavourable one.

Both can be true. What they cannot produce together is a defined-risk special situation. The
distance from $41.37 to a defensible $29 floor is 30%; the distance to a base case that
survives the contract structure is about 18% the other way. That is the wrong shape.

---

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict

Trajectory: **strengthening** on operations. Every physical milestone has been met and the
commodity is at a yearly high. The business is getting better.

The moat is **narrow but widening**: a regulatory-licence and scale-cost position as the sole
integrated United States producer, deepened by the ten-year government contract and by the
heavy rare-earth circuit coming online in mid-2026. No structural force threatens the
terminal value; the threat is Chinese price warfare, which the price-protection agreement
specifically neutralises, so the secular risk is manageable rather than material.

**The single thing the director must weigh before sizing:** the downside floor in the board
file does not exist. It is an estimate, not an asset value, and the honest floor is nearer
$29 - roughly 30% below the current price - anchored on the government's own $30.03 cost
basis rather than on anything on the balance sheet. Combine that with a value-realising event
in 2028 and a contract that hands the government 30% of commodity upside and half of magnet
profits above a threshold, and the asymmetry this funnel is designed to buy is simply not
present at $41.37. The right posture is patience with a named level, not a position.
